subject: [Elevate Health] Trial charter + KPI map and next steps

Subject: [Elevate Health] Trial charter + KPI map and next steps

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet the team. Short recap below and a recommended trial charter so we can get to a 2-week sandbox kickoff quickly. TL;DR: the trial we discussed is a 2-week pilot (sandbox) -> 4-week data collection window -> acceptance review.

Call highlights / constraints
- Primary use: clinical note summarization + triage suggestions for RN team.
- Expected traffic during pilot: ~25–75 requests/minute during working hours, spiking to 150 req/min for batch runs.
- Data sensitivity: PHI-lite (no full PHI in payload), customer requires VPC option once we move to dedicated.

Proposed success criteria (we can adjust):
1) Latency: p95 generation latency <= 350 ms for the canonical prompt shape (avg prompt ~150 tokens).
2) Throughput: steady-state 100 req/s with 5% error budget; burst handling to 500 concurrent in <3s scale-up.
3) Cost: target average inference cost <= $0.002 per token (approx $2 per 1k tokens) for the chosen model/config.
4) Quality: >= 88% intent/label match on a 500-sample human-eval set (scored by customer raters) OR no more than 6% critical failures in triage output.

Evaluation plan (what success looks like)
- Week 0 (prep): Redwood provides a sandbox endpoint + sample workload template (attached). Customer provides 500 labeled samples for blind quality eval.
- Weeks 1–2 (sandbox): Run representative traffic; we collect latency/throughput traces and token costs; we run the 500-sample eval at day 10.
- Week 3 (run validation): Iterate on model variant/quantization (if needed) and re-run the 500-sample eval.
- Week 4 (decision): Acceptance meeting; pass = recommend production pilot; fail = list of remediation actions and extension plan.

Owners / asks (first pass)
- Rishi (Sales) — overall trial owner, timeline shepherd, acceptance call.
- Ben (Infra/CS Tech) — technical contact for endpoint setup, batching, KV cache config.
- Monica (Customer Success) — onboarding, quality labeling coordination, and scheduling raters.
- Sarah / Omar (Elevate) — provide 500 labeled samples, define critical-failure examples, choose start date.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Elevate confirms start week (we propose week of Aug 24).
2) Elevate sends the 500-sample CSV & critical failure rubric (by Aug 17).
3) Redwood shares sandbox endpoint + trial runbook + calendar invites (by Aug 19).

Attachments: POC-sample-workload.csv (template), Redwood-POC-Template.pdf (trial charter).

If that looks right I’ll lock in week-of-Aug-24 as the start and loop in infra to provision the sandbox.

— Rishi

Thanks Rishi — useful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- The workload estimate is good; the 150 req/min spike is for end-of-day batch ingestion windows and is expected for 3–4 days/month.
- For quality, the team prefers an endpoint-level intent match metric + a small open-text spot-check for safety categories. Can we combine both (intent match >= 88% AND no more than 5% safety flags)?

We can commit to the 500 labeled samples but need two weeks to extract/label correctly — target delivery Aug 21. Week of Aug 24 works for kickoff.

Also looping Omar (CTO) — Omar, we discussed a VPC option once we move to a dedicated setup.

Quick technical notes — hi team, Ben here. Happy to own the infra side. A few implementation notes and a suggested runbook slice: 

Notes
- For the p95 latency target we recommend starting with a quantized model (int8) and the following config: 8-request batching window (100ms) and KV cache warmup in the first 2 minutes. That should keep p95 below 350ms for the 150-token gen case.
- Throughput: 100 req/s steady is achievable on a single dedicated 16-GPU pool depending on prompt length; for spikes we recommend auto-burst policy to a secondary pool and a fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant.
- Cost: Cost per token will vary by model; we’ll instrument token accounting in the sandbox to report daily averages.

Suggested runbook (high level)
- Day -4: Redwood provisions sandbox endpoint and shares credentials; Elevate confirms sample CSV structure.
- Day 0: Baseline smoke tests (latency/throughput).
- Day 3: First 24-hour production-like run; collect telemetry and token accounting.
- Day 7: Human-eval run on a 250-sample slice, feedback loop for model/temperature settings.
- Day 11: Full 500-sample blind eval and pass/fail decision.

I’ll add detailed test scripts to trial-runbook-draft.md and attach. If we need a shorter batching window we can tune to favor latency at slight cost increase.

-ben
